checks.name: identity
checks.reason: Rounded upright dragon retains amber eyes, orange horns and spines, cream belly, two small wings and a long tail.

checks.name: appearance
checks.reason: Green scaled surfaces and friendly stylized proportions match the requested appearance. No hair or fur is required.

checks.name: framing
checks.reason: Full body, horns, feet and wings remain inside the sampled frames; the long tail is visible in the alternate rest view and bow samples.

checks.name: deformation
checks.reason: At 0.8 and 1.5 seconds, the muzzle and mouth visibly pinch and collapse beneath the eyes instead of retaining the intact head shape during the bow.

limitations: Contact sheets cannot establish continuous motion, collision freedom, ground forces or seamless loops.
Idle changes are too subtle in the supplied images to establish the requested torso sway and tail-tip movement visually.
Supplied structural and attribute proofs report success but do not establish visual deformation quality; the target runtime remains unverified.
Hidden surfaces, rig placement and physical scale are authored assumptions.
required_repairs: Repair head and neck skin weights so the muzzle, eyes and jaw move together without facial collapse during the bow; distribute the shallow bend through the torso and neck.
Make idle torso sway and tail-tip movement visibly readable while preserving gentle motion and planted feet.
Provide updated motion evidence for the repaired idle and bow, including a view that exposes the tail and facial silhouette.

state_reviews.reason: Samples appear essentially unchanged; neither torso sway nor tail-tip movement is clearly readable. Reported numerical displacement does not resolve that visual gap.
Head orientation visibly changes toward each side and returns, with slight upper-body follow and apparently stationary feet.
Both wings visibly alternate raised and lowered positions while the dragon remains standing.
Head lowering and a sideways tail flourish visibly change geometry and return toward standing, but facial collapse undermines the requested happy shallow bow.

review.summary: Identity and framing pass, but bow deformation needs repair and idle motion lacks sufficient visible evidence.
